clue.text: Forceful machine one steered in quiet waterway

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
to steer is to lead, past tense
p for piano, the musical direction for soft
a natural waterway

explanation.surface: A forceful vessel someone guided along a peaceful canal or stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' is the musical p, for piano, a convention worth learning; 'in' puts the steering phrase between it and the waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile driver is heavy equipment that hammers posts into the ground with great force.

clue.text: Quiz round avoided by learner

indicators.note: something avoided is left out, so the learner's symbol is dropped from the word for round

blocks.note: round as in chubby, well-rounded
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A pub quiz round that a novice chose to skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiz round' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the verb quiz alone; PLUMP loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to question them persistently for information, the verb sense of interrogate.

clue.text: Weariness in tips from orator after speech giving age away

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends, so only its outermost letters are kept
giving something away means losing it, so those three letters are removed from the word before
'after' places the speaker's ends behind the shortened word for speech

blocks.note: speech as a mode of communication
taken as written, and removed
first and last letters of orator

explanation.surface: An audience flagging as a long-winded speaker drones on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' means both ends of orator, not just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a pleasant or listless lack of energy, close in sense to tiredness and lethargy.

clue.text: Lacy blue dress designed for dancer

indicators.note: something designed is made up from raw material, so these letters are rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: the thirteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A frilly blue costume created specially for a ballerina.
explanation.walkthrough: Darcey Bussell is a famous British ballerina, a former principal of the Royal Ballet and later a judge on the TV show Strictly Come Dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a celebrated principal ballerina, so she is an example of a professional performer of ballet.

clue.text: Diplomacy without force supported by northern church, basically

indicators.note: 'without' means lacking, so the letter for force is taken out of the word for diplomacy
in a down entry, being supported means sitting on top, so the northern church letters come underneath

blocks.note: finesse is tact and skill in handling people
F is the physics symbol for force
N abbreviates northern
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A tactful approach backed by a church in the north, fundamentally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: FINESSE loses its F to give INESSE, with N and CE placed below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean fundamentally, describing the essential nature of something rather than its details.

clue.text: Colour that is picked up in bird frequenting coastal area

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it, so the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a basic colour
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: Spotting a flash of colour on a seabird by the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: RED followed by IE, read upwards, gives EIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck found along northern shorelines, prized for its soft down.

clue.text: See second best round

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the word for best is written backwards

blocks.note: S abbreviates second
top as in finest, the best

explanation.surface: Watching a boxer who came second-best in a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice or catch sight of it, a synonym of the verb see.

clue.text: Point about staff copper raised, getting result

indicators.note: in a down clue something raised is lifted upward, so the chemical symbol is read bottom to top
'about' means surrounding, so the abbreviation for point goes around the rest

blocks.note: PT abbreviates point
a staff is a rod or stick
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer lifted with a stick, leading to an outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, whose symbol comes from Latin cuprum.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is the outcome or consequence of a process, as in the product of hard work.

clue.text: Aimed at gain in trade all over the place

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered and disordered, so these letters are jumbled
'in' puts the word for gain inside the jumbled letters

blocks.note: to gain is to get
the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A business pursued its profits in a chaotic market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trade' looks like part of the picture, but it is the jumbled fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be targeted is to be singled out as the object of an attack or campaign.

clue.text: House style according to declaration

indicators.note: a declaration is something spoken out, so the word for style is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a manner is a way or style of doing something

explanation.surface: Describing the design of a home, as someone has stated it.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country residence, historically the main dwelling of a landed estate.

clue.text: Scrambled over a dune, making an effort

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, so the article is part of the definition: an effort is an endeavour

indicators.note: scrambled means jumbled up, like scrambled eggs, so the following letters are mixed

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone clambering hard up a sandy hill, really trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrambled' paints climbing a dune, but it signals the letters are jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt or exertion towards a goal, the same as a serious try.

clue.text: Compromise? Hotel for instance offers it

blocks.note: first meaning: a settlement or agreement reached by give and take
second meaning: rooms and lodging provided for guests

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark links the two halves as if a hotel offers compromise; they are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both reaching an agreement with others and the rooms a hotel provides to guests.

clue.text: Part of building above foundations getting great new rust remedy - about time

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters of the word for corrosion are reordered

blocks.note: super means great, excellent
the letters to be rearranged
a cure is a remedy
T abbreviates time

explanation.surface: A building's upper part treated with a terrific new anti-rust product, eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: The time letter goes just after the first letter of the remedy word, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstructure is everything built on top of a base or foundation, such as the upper storeys.

clue.text: Roll into hearing in court

indicators.note: 'into' tells us one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a bread roll is a bun
a court hearing is a trial

explanation.surface: Someone tumbling into a courtroom session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like a verb of falling, but it is the bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body set up to judge disputes, a kind of court or judicial panel.

clue.text: Garland around tree’s not normally seen in city

indicators.note: something not in its normal state is disarranged, so these letters change order

blocks.note: a lei is a Hawaiian flower garland
c for circa, Latin for around
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusual wreath around a tree, rarely spotted in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like a container signal, but it gives C, short for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester is a large city in the East Midlands of England.

clue.text: Dull affair having no end

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter of the word for affair is cut off

blocks.note: an affair is a matter, a business

explanation.surface: A boring relationship that just drags on endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affair' suggests romance, but it means a matter or business.
explanation.definitionFit: Matte describes a surface or finish that is not shiny, so it is lacking lustre.

clue.text: Definite corruption of cruel act

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Clear-cut means sharply defined and unambiguous, leaving no doubt.

clue.text: Reel around in circles

blocks.note: a reel of thread or film is a spool

explanation.surface: Staggering dizzily round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reel around' paints dizziness; reel is the noun, a spool.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops are curves that turn back on themselves, so they are rings or circles.

clue.text: Choose centre for holiday with mother? Perfect

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: to opt is to choose
the middle of the seven letters of holiday
mum is the informal British word for mother

explanation.surface: Picking a holiday resort with Mum along: ideal?
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the best possible, so as an adjective it means ideal or flawless.

clue.text: Final section from record, one left by villain, not right

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The closing part of a crime story in which a single person is abandoned by the baddie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left by' reads as abandoned by, but left is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the concluding part added at the end of a book, play or speech.

clue.text: Universal fury about doctor causing offence

blocks.note: U is the British film rating for universal
rage is fury
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Widespread anger at a physician who has upset people.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate for Universal, suitable for all ages; 'about' makes the first two words wrap the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so umbrage is resentment at a perceived insult.

clue.text: Heat’s damaged container, perhaps, depending on circumstances

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

maybe means perhaps

clue.text: False name, sadly, one admitted

blocks.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow, sadly
Roman numeral for one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' looks like an anagram signal, but it gives ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name used to hide one's true identity.

clue.text: Garment in attractive style

blocks.note: the end of attractive and the start of style

explanation.definitionFit: A vest is an item of clothing worn on the upper body, an undershirt or waistcoat.

clue.text: Bed occupied by male with obvious illness

clue.text: Weighty book from my perspective
